title: Undated Abdulrazzak respiratory paper
note: Seven preferred images forwarded from a 2025-01-05 post; this is provenance, not a verified exam date. All 36 supplied items retained with section numbering. Highlighting and stars are unofficial source marks. The archive's Sarwar recaptures are redundant versions and not additional questions.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following happens during inspiration?
options: The anterior-posterior dimension of the chest is decreased.
The vertical dimension of the thorax is increased
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Diaphragm descent increases the vertical dimension of the chest.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is correct about "Transpulmonary Pressure (TPP)"?
options: TPP = pleural pressure minus alveolar pressure
At the beginning of the expiration is equal to +7.5 cm of water
At the beginning of inspiration is equal to -5 cm of water
TPP = alveolar pressure minus atmospheric pressure
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: TPP is alveolar minus pleural pressure; at end inspiration/start expiration it is about +7.5 cmH2O in the reference model.

questions.prompt: Compared to other gases, which gas has the highest diffusing capacity during exercise?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: CO2 has much greater tissue diffusion capacity than O2 or CO due to its higher solubility.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is NOT correct about pulmonary circulation?
options: Vasodilation occurs in response to hypoxia
Supplies blood flow to respiratory zone
The mean pulmonary arterial pressure is 15 mm Hg
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Alveolar hypoxia causes local pulmonary vasoconstriction, not dilation.

questions.prompt: What is the value of "O2 utilization coefficient" in a normal person?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The usual resting reference is approximately 25% extraction of arterial oxygen content.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is correct about blood flow at the "top of the lung" during exercise?
options: The blood flow is zone-1 type
Blood flow will only be maintained during systole
There is a continuous blood flow during both systole and diastole
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Exercise raises vascular pressures and recruits apical vessels, converting intermittent zone-2 flow toward continuous zone-3 flow.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following leads to an increase in airway resistance?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Cold air can provoke reflex bronchoconstriction; VIP is a bronchodilator.

questions.prompt: The right main bronchus is a part of ...
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Main bronchi conduct air without alveolar exchange and contribute to anatomical dead space. The source typo death space is retained.

questions.prompt: Which one the following volumes or capacity is more than others in the lung?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Standard reference values rank IRV (about 3000 mL) above FRC, RV and ERV; this is a reference comparison, not a universal individual measurement.

questions.prompt: With a duration of 1.5 seconds for inspiration phase, what will be the duration of Ramp Signal?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The inspiratory ramp lasts through the stated inspiratory period, 1.5 seconds.

questions.prompt: To measure which lung volume or capacity, it is necessary to use the "diluting helium" method?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: TLC includes RV, which simple spirometry cannot measure. Helium dilution is one available method, not the only possible method.

questions.prompt: Which factor does not play a role in the transport of CO2?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Carboxyhemoglobin refers to CO binding. Carbonic anhydrase, hemoglobin buffering and oxygenation-dependent Haldane effects participate in normal CO2 transport.

questions.prompt: Which gas is used for estimating of "diffusing capacity of O2" in the lung?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: CO uptake is used in the clinical diffusing-capacity test and can be related to O2 diffusion in the textbook model.

questions.prompt: What is the "Anatomical shunt" in the lung?
options: A decrease in ventilation/perfusion ratio (VA/Q) to zero
An increase in VA/Q ratio 10 times more than normal amount
A fall in O2 pressure of arterial blood caused by venous admixture
A decrease in the cardiac output to half
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: C best describes the consequence of anatomical venous admixture, though it is not a complete anatomical definition. A denotes physiological shunting through unventilated units.

questions.prompt: What is the difference in CO2 pressure of venous blood and arterial blood?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The usual mixed-venous minus arterial PCO2 gradient is approximately 5-6 mmHg; 5 is the closest supplied teaching value.

questions.prompt: What is the main source for H+ production to stimulate the neurons in the chemosensitive area?
options: An increase in blood CO2 pressure
An increase in blood hydrogen ion concentration
A reduction in blood O2 pressure
An increase in pH of intercellular fluids
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: CO2 crosses into brain/CSF and generates H+, the central chemosensitive stimulus.

questions.prompt: Which one the following leads to an increase in affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Reduced 2,3-DPG/BPG shifts the curve left and increases oxygen affinity.

questions.prompt: The content of which of the following in venous red blood cells is greater than that of arterial red blood cells?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: C is the intended chloride-shift answer, but the unrestricted wording also permits increased carbonic acid and intracellular bicarbonate with higher venous PCO2. No uniquely correct chemical-species comparison is established.

questions.prompt: Which one the following is correct about the role of the dorsal respiratory group in medulla?
options: Inhibits the pneumotaxic center in pons
Sends its action potentials to phrenic nerves
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: D is the intended description of inspiratory drive relayed through phrenic motor pathways. DRG is not confined to deep inspiration; neural control is distributed.

questions.prompt: Which one the following is correct about ventilation and perfusion in the lungs?
options: The ventilation increases from top of the lung to bottom
The blow flow decreases from top of the lung to bottom
The ventilation to perfusion ratio (V/Q) increases from top of the lung to bottom
V/Q ratio is same for all levels of the lung in upright person
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In an upright lung both ventilation and perfusion increase toward the base, with perfusion increasing more; V/Q therefore decreases.

questions.prompt: Pulmonary surfactant:
options: Leads to a decreases in respiratory work
Is produced in type I alveolar cells
Is in part composed of NaCl
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Surfactant lowers surface tension and inflation work; type II cells produce it. NaCl is not its defining surface-active component.

questions.prompt: Which one the following factor has effect on distribution of pulmonary blood flow in the lung?
options: Elastin and collagen in lung parenchyma
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Gravity is the direct determinant in the standard regional-flow comparison. Both B and D carry green highlighting; no single providedKey is assigned. Other options can have indirect pathological effects.

questions.prompt: All the following bones are involved in the formation of the medial wall of the nose except...
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Lacrimal forms part of the lateral wall, not the septal/medial wall.

questions.prompt: Which of the following arteries branches from the ophthalmic artery?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Anterior ethmoidal arises from ophthalmic; the remaining options are external-carotid system branches.

questions.prompt: All the following options are correct except......
options: The maxillary sinus open to the superior meatus
The ethmoidal bulla is located at a lower level than the middle concha.
The nasolacrimal duct open to the inferior meatus
The group of middle Ethmoidal cells opens to the middle meatus.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The maxillary sinus drains into the middle meatus via the semilunar hiatus, not the superior meatus.

questions.prompt: All the following structures are adjacent to the front of the trachea except...?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Thoracic duct lies posteriorly in the mediastinum, not anterior to the trachea.

questions.prompt: All of the following options are characteristics of the parietal plura except....?
options: It is innervated by sympathic nerves.
It does not penetrate into the grooves of the lung.
The lower end of the parietal plura in the mid axilary line, is at the level of the 10th rib
Parietal plura is going to form pulmonary ligament
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Parietal pleural sensation uses intercostal and phrenic nerves. Pleural reflections form the pulmonary ligament; visceral pleura follows lung fissures.

questions.prompt: All the following options are correct about the main right bronchus except...?
options: It is thicker than the left main broncus
It is shorter than the left main bronchus
Compared to the left main bronchus, it is farther from the midline
Before penetrating the umbilicus of the right lung, it is divided
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The right main bronchus is more vertical and nearer the midline; it gives the upper-lobe bronchus before the hilum.

questions.prompt: Which of the following makes false vocal fold?
options: The upper side of the cricothyroid memberane (or conus elasticus).
The lower side of the cricothyroid memberane (or conus elasticus).
The upper edge of the quadrangular membrane
The lower edge of the quadrangular membrane.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The inferior free margin of the quadrangular membrane forms the vestibular ligament in the false fold.

questions.prompt: All of the following are true in relation to the internal laryngeal nerve except:
options: It is one of the two terminal branches of the superior laryngeal nerve
It provides the sensation of the laryngeal mucosa below the real vocal folds.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Internal laryngeal sensation is above the vocal folds; below them the recurrent laryngeal nerve supplies sensation.

questions.prompt: Which of the muscles of the larynx causes abduction of the true vocal cords?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Posterior cricoarytenoid is the principal vocal-fold abductor.

questions.prompt: All of the following muscle attached to muscular process except,,,,?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The source selects cricothyroid (D), which has no arytenoid attachment. However, transverse arytenoid (A) attaches to posterior arytenoid surfaces rather than specifically to the muscular process; posterior cricoarytenoid and oblique arytenoid do use that process. The precise stem therefore permits A and D and is not single-answer safe.

questions.prompt: In microscopic structure Which of the following is observed bowman glands?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Bowman serous glands occur in olfactory lamina propria.

questions.prompt: In microscopic structure Which part of air duct of respiratory system is observed bundle of elastic fiber?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Source selects larynx, consistent with elastic vocal ligaments, but bronchial walls also contain elastic fibers. Without a named ligament or arrangement, the stem is not uniquely localizing.

questions.prompt: In microscopic structure which part of lobules Lung is observed simple esquamose epithelial tissue?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Alveoli and the alveolar openings lining ducts have squamous type I epithelium; respiratory bronchioles also contain alveolar interruptions. A and D are both defensible, so no single answer is assigned.

questions.prompt: which part of microscopic structure long tissue is observed pneumocytes type III?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The marked alveolar-space answer suggests the source uses type III for alveolar macrophages. That label is nonstandard and unsupported by the review; macrophages are not epithelial pneumocytes.

audit.notes: All preferred source images visually reviewed; OCR used only as a drafting aid. All supplied complete items retained. Source annotations are unofficial, preserved separately from the audited answer. Null audited keys deliberately quarantine ambiguous or defective questions. Numbered options 1-4 and Persian letters are normalized to A-D in displayed order.
